newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Namibia's Nujoma says SADC trade barriers must go.
newsitem.headline: Namibia's Nujoma says SADC trade barriers must go.

text.p: Namibian President Sam Nujoma on Monday urged further dismantling of cross-border trade, transport and investment barriers in southern Africa to encourage private sector business.
"We must continue to dismantle barriers to trade and investment even if there might occur some short-term costs," Nujoma told a business conference in Botswana.

Leaders from seven of the 12-member Southern African Development Community (SADC) are attending the 'Smart Partnerships' conference in Kasane to promote closer ties between government and the private sector.
The SADC comprises Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe.
Nujoma said the region should share resources to help develop social contacts and partnerships.
"Instead of doing things on our own, we must share our resources," he said.
He said road, rail and air links in southern Africa should be fully utilised and cooperation in trade, transport and investment encouraged.
For the first time, the region was poised to reap the full benefits of its rich resources but could not do so without attracting globally competitive companies, Nujoma said.

"We need to fast-track industrial development by bringing both high-tech and appropriate technology to our shores. We do not have time to ride the learning curve which others have done before us," he said.
